author: Claude (English teacher role)
basis: Trimmed from the original A2 column of sheet 'SDG 13-1', which averaged 40.3 words per slide — longer than the B1 and B2 versions and above the A2 ceiling. Wording, order and every fact are kept; only padding is removed. Band: 26-35 words, 7-12 words per sentence, FK 3-7.

slides.1: Our summers are getting very long and hot. The world has a big climate problem. We see bad storms and melting ice. Today, let us talk about how we save our planet.
slides.2: What is SDG 13? It means Climate Action. It asks every country to cut dirty air and prepare for disasters. If we do not act now, our cities will be in danger.
slides.3: Look at Taiwan. We are a small island, so typhoons and rising seas hurt us easily. Our high-tech factories also use a lot of electricity. How can we help the world?
slides.4: Taiwan is getting hot faster than other places. This is a scary fact. It changes our food and our clean water. We must find a good solution very quickly.
slides.5: Here is the main problem. Taiwan uses too much coal and oil, and these make dirty air. Our chip factories need power all the time. How can we stop the pollution?
slides.6: We must ask some hard questions today. Is our high-energy life safe for the future? Can we change to green power fast enough? Students and scientists must answer them.
slides.7: But there is good news. Taiwan made a new climate law. Our goal is Net Zero by 2050. Now companies must pay money if they make too much dirty air.
slides.8: We can see big changes. There are many new wind turbines in the sea, and our wind power is growing fast. Schools and factories also put solar panels on their roofs.
slides.9: People in Taiwan are very good at recycling. We ride the MRT and Ubike every day. Green living is popular now. But is recycling enough? We need bigger changes too.
slides.10: How can science help Taiwan? We are building smart grids. They use AI to share electricity. This technology stops energy waste and makes our power system work better.
slides.11: Another cool invention is carbon capture. Scientists catch bad air from factory chimneys before it goes into the sky. Then they hide it deep underground. This science really helps.
slides.12: Think about our streets. Taiwan is famous for electric scooters. They use batteries, not gasoline. This smart design stops dirty air and loud noise in crowded cities.
slides.13: However, being green is not easy. New technology is very expensive. Small shops worry they cannot pay. How can we help everyone buy green things? Nobody should be left behind.
slides.14: Energy safety is a big debate now. Our tech factories need stable power every hour. But wind and solar need good weather. Should we use nuclear power or gas?
slides.15: Climate change has no borders. Taiwan has great technology, and we want to share it. Politics can be difficult, but we must work together. A storm hurts everyone.
slides.16: Finally, we must be careful. Some companies lie about being green. We call this greenwashing. As students, we must check the data and ask about their promises.
slides.17: To sum up, Taiwan is doing a good job. We have laws, wind power, and smart technology. We are changing from a dirty island into a green leader.
slides.18: Why does this matter to you? Because you are the future. You can study science and invent better tools. You can also save energy at home and speak up.
slides.19: Do not be afraid of the climate crisis. Feel excited to help! Taiwan has smart people and kind hearts. Innovation is our strength. Let us build a clean world.
slides.20: The clock is ticking. The Earth is calling for help. Will you be part of the solution? Taiwan is ready for SDG 13, and so am I. Thank you for listening.
